### E173 protected popup explicit navigation and document rearm

Protected popup goto/back/forward/reload now use the existing shared worker and
original Source/Handoff instead of attempting ordinary network Slot admission.
A viewless navigation ticket queues only metadata registration against the
already-cached Source binding. Its original pump issues the command once,
collects ACK/native commitment and services the original downloads. Cancellation
remains stop data. A late receipt never upgrades a cancelled operation.

The metadata registration operation is explicitly non-owning: a queued timeout
or cancellation cannot close a healthy physical Source binding whose wire that
operation never touched. Deterministic barriers on the same existing executor
prove both queued paths, zero original navigation commands and successful new
navigation on the retained connection. There is no second executor, reconnect,
replacement native view or Fetch guard. Waiting for native replies yields to
the shared receive pump; claiming progress on every pending turn had starved
receipts in the initial implementation and was corrected before this commit.

The actual UI navigation record now reconciles original native commitment with
the current UI epoch/profile/channel. A fresh document marker and exact Handoff
proof are checked against the native frame, loader and destination before world
inventory and again afterwards. A late WebView page callback can revalidate a
new UI epoch against that same commit; it does not repeat navigation. Definite
no-effect/negative-ACK outcomes permit explicit original-page inventory recovery.
Unknown sent effects remain uncertain. The frame command route now supports the
guarded document read for this original navigation reference; older references
are refused before metadata I/O. The explicit popup navigation denials are removed;
protected takeover/release remains unavailable pending its lifecycle join.

Integration also caught a shared history-read bug: the default frame job has a
10-second budget, while each native RPC accepts at most5 seconds. History
document verification forwarded the whole remaining budget and rejected valid
reads as `cdp_arguments_invalid`. That fixed proof read now caps its RPC slice
without changing the enclosing deadline. Product goto/back/forward/reload followed
by default-budget, navigation-pinned frame reads exercises the correction.

Eleven added cases cover native UI ticket flow, deterministic queued cancellation/
timeout and recovery, sent cancellation/late ACK, pending-download denial, actual
product four-command document rearm, late page callback, mismatched loader,
cancel, rejection/inventory recovery and ACK without native commitment. The flow
also rejects all three older navigation references before protocol snapshots.
No Agent evaluation is performed by these metadata/world qualification cases.
The native source/worker/reservation/navigation/frame/document fragments are
actual product code; UI/profile/renderer surroundings remain controlled.

### E179 guarded navigation overlap and download-only recovery coverage

Added two actual product-fragment/common-worker/JVM/JNI acceptance paths; no
product code change was needed. These are controlled renderer/UI peers, not
Android framework, installed-provider or physical-device qualification.

`preparation-page-navigation-overlap` holds the first original native ACK and
verifies that a second navigation is rejected before sending. It then releases
that ACK, holds the original isolated-world reply after its native commit, and
starts a second accepted navigation. Releasing the old world reply cannot
publish the old document or disturb the second navigation. The new document
becomes readable, the old navigation reference is refused before new inventory,
and the new reference remains usable. Exactly two navigation commands/two new
worlds, zero page evaluations, one Browser connection and one native proof
connection are checked. This path passes55 reported checks.

`preparation-page-navigation-from-download` starts with the original protected

### E180 fixed original attachment retirement for human-control integration

Current protected-popup disposal waits for native destruction/detach. Human
takeover must keep the actual page alive instead. Added the internal Session
primitive needed for an explicit protocol detach of that original attachment;
it is not a public command, a native ownership grant or a completed takeover
coordinator. `popup_takeover_unqualified` and public Android automation remain
unchanged until the entire physical-owner/source/return-control join is proved.

`detachProtectedAttachment` accepts only the Session's retained, protected,
activated original event and a live internal quiescence permit. There is no
caller-supplied target ID, URL, script or general RPC. It rejects unactivated,
foreign, stale, invalid-budget, lost-permit and reentrant scopes before sending.
Pending original requests/responses, offers, body streams, cleanup controls and
navigation prevent detachment. These checks use the original attachment's scope,
so another attachment's independent body need not be cancelled or awaited.
The caller must still prove physical human ownership and descendant cleanup;
this primitive cannot establish either fact by itself.

empty command reply records only `retirementAcknowledged`; it does not invent a
native `Target.detachedFromTarget` event, source release or body/stream cleanup.
Malformed replies, provider rejection/unsupported, timeout, transport failure and
lost ownership retain their sanitized original cause and possible-effect flag.
No failed or uncertain attempt is resent. The coordinator must separately join
its authentic native event and original transfer cleanup before rearm.

### E182 original human-owned leaf protocol retirement

Connected the exact physical human-transfer receipt to the original product
PopupNetwork and its existing Browser worker. The internal coordinator first
quiesces unfinished downloads, preserving the user cancellation cause and already
completed original bytes, then transfers the exact native owner and retires its
page/source markers. It requests a one-use typed retirement; no UI boolean,
caller-selected target, URL, script, second Browser wire or replacement WebView
can assert that cleanup is complete.

The worker requires the exact Promotion's completed human transfer/end receipt,
an independently finished original Source close, its original disconnected and
quiescing download Connection and clean source receipts. Document peers revoke
old authority. Existing nested document sessions are explicitly rejected with
`cdp_popup_human_descendants_unqualified`; their native cleanup is not inferred
from a cleared registry. Only a leaf reaches E180's fixed original detach, whose
per-attachment pending request/response/offer/body/control/navigation checks
still apply. Other work on the original serialized wire is not replaced.

The original detach ACK and authenticated native detached event join separately.
An ACK without the native event cannot finish the human row. An event without
the ACK cannot finish it either. Rejection, unsupported commands, malformed ACK,
lost ACK and wrong-session events retain sanitized original causes, protocol
codes and possible-effect flags without replay. Uncertain shared-wire cleanup
keeps its process guard fenced; native page preservation does not declare that
global state clean. A real later physical page destruction can independently
finish that row's native teardown, which is distinct from shared-wire recovery.

A successfully retired human row keeps the same native view, profile/quota and
download controller/catalog. Complete source bytes remain verified and readable
with the same download ID and charged quota. Pending/streaming sources cancel as
user decisions and must acknowledge original abort/I/O cleanup before detach.
On actual later physical destruction, retained cached files are released even
when protocol cleanup is uncertain. This fixes otherwise retained human cache
files while preserving the independent protocol fence. The old Handoff,
Promotion, world and marker authority never revive.

The toolbar previously merged any fulfilled takeover/return result into page
state. Android's structured failed return therefore made `state.error` an object,
hid the physical webpage, displayed an unhelpful object string and could break
the subsequent browser report. The same unchecked fulfilled result allowed the
file-picker/dialog helper to continue after a failed takeover.

explicit boolean `manual` matching the requested control direction, without a
failure/error, changes UI ownership. Unrelated receipt fields cannot replace
page URL/loading/error state. Canonical native refusals get bounded Chinese
recovery text; structured network cleanup is reported independently as confirmed
or unconfirmed. Diagnostics retain only the bounded control code/command/typed
cleanup receipt. A control failure remains a control notice, never a page-load
error, and sends no automatic retry, navigation, close or create.

control disables the toolbar and current menu entry, preserves original manual
state and blocks duplicate native dispatch. A state read dispatched before a
control command, or delivered while its original receipt is pending, cannot
overwrite that receipt. This also suppresses stale rejected reads from turning
a newer successful control change into a page error. Native ownership remains
authoritative; UI validation does not expand Agent permission or Android gates.

### E187 release confirmed terminal sources after UI delivery abandonment

Follow-up to E186's retained generic sources found a deterministic lifecycle
defect. Network Slot.drop marked terminal delivery abandoned but invoked release
only when it removed a still-queued task. If the original worker exit had already
finished that source, release previously saw terminalDelivered=false. The later
UI drop changed it to true without revisiting release; no worker remained to
remove the confirmed terminal row. Both native close and Session close could be
confirmed while networkPending still retained that source indefinitely.

The witness uses the actual public worker shutdown, the existing original
executor and a one-shot controlled Ui.remove callback. That callback reenters
shutdown and waits for the actual worker-exit finally before the outer shutdown
continues to its second source. It does not set private product state or create
another protocol worker. Old code fails with stage=3/TERMINAL, cancelled=true,
cleanupFailed=false, terminalDelivered=true, connectionClose=2 and sessionClose=2.
See `.mdo/E187-terminal-drop-red.log`. This proves a real ordering defect with
the same retained-source symptom as the earlier UI-loss observation. The older
failure did not record per-slot state, so this is not an exclusive historical
root-cause claim.

Slot.drop now invokes the existing guarded release after marking delivery
abandoned and removing its callback, including when worker exit already made it
terminal. Queued removal still makes only an unexecuted task terminal. The
release predicate still requires TERMINAL plus abandoned/delivered completion
and no cleanup failure; active I/O, closing/native-pending state and failed
native cleanup are not freed or reported successful. A concurrent later finish
also revisits the same predicate, covering both orders without reconnect/retry.

Two deterministic shutdown variants add 32 checks: both native connections close
successfully and all rows disappear, or one native close fails and exactly that
source remains fenced. Each native close runs once; no late UI completion is
invented. Five focused two-case invocations pass, the complete generic network
worker passes 300 checks versus the prior 268, and the old quiescence-ui-loss
case passes ten targeted invocations after the fix. Earlier pending-close and
failure receipt cases remain active in that same generic worker gate.

### E188 require original native descendant receipts after document retirement

The controlled original-worker witness reproduces premature cleanup in the old
product: its root native detach sets Handoff.detached and releases the candidate
while its two previously attached native iframe sessions have not supplied detach
receipts. DocumentPeer.retire also erased the data-child map used by the old human
descendant refusal. See `.mdo/E188-native-ledger-red.log`; it runs the actual old
Session/Broker against the new fixture in the same fixed output directory. The
reviewed sources were restored only after that check terminated.

DocumentPeer now keeps bounded original native session/parent records separately
from its document/data children. Data cancellation clears listeners and document/data-child admission while
preserving those cleanup obligations. Session.fenceChild
allows only the original native Target attachment/detachment events; ordinary
late replies and DOM traffic stay retired. A parent detach is retained as a
routing ancestor until its children also detach. The root receipt revokes the
original authority immediately, but final Handoff.detached/candidate release
requires every retained native descendant receipt. Unknown/duplicate receipts
cannot clear another owner, incorrect parent/owner events fail closed, and a
new attachment from a natively detached parent is rejected. The native registry
is capped at 64; Session lifetime/seen-child bounds remain in force.

Resetting a document no longer treats the fixed disable ACK as evidence that all
native children detached. This separation follows the reviewed
[official Target protocol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-protocol/master/pdl/domains/Target.pdl);
the ACK and each original native notification remain independent receipts.
Human takeover still refuses unqualified descendants, including after an
in-flight original document call cancels and removes its data children.

Full validation also exposed an adjacent shared-wire regression: a native child
detach could end its pending attached RPC while its root was still live, causing
the old generic incomplete-RPC path to close the wire for another page. The
ancestry-validating broker now records that exact native child detach; only
cdp_session_detached for that attached call may abandon its reply without closing
the shared wire. Ordinary mismatches, transport failures and unproved detach
claims retain failure behavior. Original effect/failure results are preserved,
late replies cannot upgrade them, and no operation is replayed.

The fixture now records actual outgoing native attachment ancestry and emits
explicit native child-detach events for its controlled provider disable/root
closure. The new delayed-receipt modes override that behavior and verify root-
first, parent-first, leaf-first, late attachment, duplicate receipt, foreign
owner, wrong ancestor, resource limit and retired-parent attachment. The tenth
new mode holds an original child RPC across human transfer and verifies native
obligations survive its cancellation. These ten modes pass 604
checks; the related eleven-mode focused run passes 669.

### E189 retire descendant RPC admission after native ancestor detach

The E188 follow-up qualification reproduces a distinct scope-retirement defect.
Hold an actual Runtime.evaluate reply from the original native leaf session and
deliver its ancestor's authentic native detach while both page owners remain
live. Frames removes the ancestor and its document descendants, but the old
DocumentPeer.retireChild removed only the local data map. The leaf remained
admitted to ordinary Session traffic, so its original RPC kept waiting for a
reply from a data scope that had already ended. See
`.mdo/E189-grandchild-red.log`; its primary assertion records that wait, with
teardown failures retained as suppressed evidence.

DocumentPeer.retireChild now fences that exact descendant's Session data
admission before removing its local record. Only cdp_session_detached on the
original attached RPC may abandon its wait when that session has explicit data
retirement or an authentic native detach receipt. This does not mark the leaf
physically detached: its independent native record and cleanup routing remain.
Late ordinary replies are discarded, the original failure/effect result remains
terminal, and foreign-source mismatches and transport failures retain rejection.
No replacement action, URL navigation or general RPC grant is introduced.

The new read and possible-effect variants target the actual leaf-frame route on
the original worker. Each verifies one failure callback and the original effect
bit while the root's physical owner stays current. They hold a second page's
actual RPC reply, deliver the old leaf reply during that call, and verify the
second page succeeds without changing the first result. After the root is
closed and its native detach arrives, cleanup must still wait for the leaf's
own native detach. Its authentic receipt finally releases the routing ancestor
and original root; another page operation and final source/guard cleanup pass.
These two modes pass 152 checks. Direct-child, parent-first
and foreign-source cases also pass in the related focused run.

## E191 — fixed root-only auto-attach retirement after data loss

Added a private native Session primitive that disables automatic attachment only
on the exact retained original root. It uses the existing serialized dispatcher
and a typed, temporary command context binding original native object, internal
fixed parameters, session and command ID. Ordinary data admission is revoked
before dispatch; only this original command's reply can cross that fence. No
generic cleanup RPC, caller-selected protocol parameters or Browser-global
disable is exposed. A native-ended original cannot dispatch; reentry and replay
are rejected. Timeout/corruption/ownership loss retain the existing fail-closed
behavior. A terminal protocol rejection preserves the other page's live wire
without restoring the old root's data authority or replaying its cleanup.

Actual ACK, descendant native events, paused request/body receipts and final root
detach remain independent. ACK success leaves retained native pauses charged and
root detach blocked until their cleanup is proved. The primitive is intentionally
not wired into the broker's public/human-retirement coordinator yet: raw paused
requests and cancelled synchronous continuation receipts still require qualified
retirement before that integration.

Thirty-six new direct original-worker cases cover both initially admitted and
already-data-fenced roots, fixed command scope/parameters, ACK before/after native
child end, late native child attachment and old data/replies, peer admission,
pending-pause retention, native end before dispatch, bad/unsupported replies,
wrong session/ID, send/timeout/ownership failures, foreign identity, reentry and
no replay. The control gate passes 4,639 checks versus 3,205 (+1,434); two real
native transport sessions remain unchanged. Preserve
`.mdo/E191-retirement-controls.log`.

## E192 — preserve original Fetch receipts after data cancellation

Reproduced an actual E191 Session defect with a sent original request, deliberate
data cancellation and its actual late same-wire ACK. The old packet path dropped
that ACK as retired data, leaving the original pause charged indefinitely. Keep
the explicit red witness in `.mdo/E192-original-flow-red.log`. The repair separates
native control receipts from the already-terminal data-call outcome; it neither
turns cancellation into success nor replays a potentially effective continuation.

The private PausedFlow identity binds the exact retained native attachment,
frozen original pause, fixed internal parameters, operation and native receipt.
The existing bounded Control[] dispatcher preserves its serial/session row across
data and native attachment retirement. Only a matching empty native success
releases that pause; a protocol rejection keeps it charged while another original
page remains usable. Mismatched/corrupt traffic and expired original deadlines
retain fail-closed behavior. No deadline is restarted or native receipt fabricated.
Pre-send cancellation removes an unissued row and records NOT_SENT, so it cannot
leave an indefinitely pending control or invent an actual send/ACK.

Added the private fixed abortProtectedPause cleanup primitive. It derives only
Fetch.failRequest/Aborted from a frozen original pause, accepts no request selector
and grants no new continuation/body/source access. Pending original controls must
finish first; a rejected continuation can be cleaned, while a sent abort cannot
be replayed. Existing body/offer/stream receipts remain independent. Cleanup-only
packet handling now retains bounded late Fetch pauses only on the exact original
protected root that has not received native end; DOM/new data stays fenced.
The broker has not adopted this primitive or E191's root auto-attach disable in
its human-retirement coordinator yet; that integration remains required.

root native detach, while preserving the other original document. Their new
proof flags are required by the final verifier; no product state is overwritten.

Two fixture scheduling assumptions were strengthened. A response pass can still

## E193 — join original human-root and native flow retirement

Reproduced two actual defects before repair. A valid raw Fetch pause between
fixed detach dispatch and ACK/native end caused cdp_owner_changed, because the
live owner predicate incorrectly rechecked pre-send quiescence. Native root end
could also mark the handoff detached while an original Fetch control remained
unacknowledged. Preserve `.mdo/E193-late-pause-red.log` and
`.mdo/E193-original-flow-join-red.log` as the explicit failing witnesses.

Session retains strict pre-send busy/native ownership checks and fences root
data before dispatch. During serialized detach the independent original owner,
not a newly arrived frozen pause, controls admission. Broker-matched authentic
root end immediately revokes data and clears raw pauses, retaining native ancestry
and issued receipt rows. The new local originalCleanupPending query remains valid
after native end. Broker finish/prune revisits original roots and waits their
actual controls/bodies/offers/auto-attach command before setting detached; the
fixed root ACK is still independently required for humanDetached. Nothing is
replayed or upgraded from a cancelled data result to successful data.

The human coordinator now retires document authority, closes the original Source,
waits transfer/body cleanup, disables only this root's child auto-attachment once,
waits authentic descendant ends, aborts frozen raw pauses and then joins original
root ACK/native end. A physical close can still win safely. Original completed
bytes/catalog/quota/profile and the human page are preserved. No Browser-global
stop, arbitrary cleanup RPC, new DOM/world/body access or replacement view is used.

Added twenty actual controlled product modes: two native-root-before-flow-ACK
orders, one late raw pause, and seventeen descendant cases covering ACK/end order,
late attachments, held ACK/child/body, completed/pending files, raw request/response
pauses, rejected/unsupported/malformed/missing/send-failed stops, missing child
and incorrect parent. Their new checks total 986.
Direct original cleanup passes 7,137 checks (+89), including two late pause cases;
the existing 42 cancelled-flow, 22 fixed-abort and three unsent cases remain.
Two real native transport sessions are unchanged. Two old descendant/in-flight
product modes intentionally change from unqualified failure to genuine successful
retirement. All prior 562 business results were compared; only their exact expected
fields changed in the final run, with no unreviewed semantic changes.
